fair_value_reason: Pro forma. EV/EBITDA: $3.05B normalized combined EBITDA (standalone ~$2.3B + AliGroup ~$0.73B + small synergies) x 5.1x = $15.6B, less net claims of ~$3.0B (net debt $4.75B + pension $0.57B - Ma'aden $1.3B - FCF $1.0B) = $12.5B / 282.8M = ~$44.3. P/E: EBITDA $3.05B - D&A $0.93B - interest $0.39B = $1.73B pretax x 0.70 = $1.21B / 282.8M = $4.28 x 9.5x = $40.7 + Ma'aden $4.6/share = ~$45.3. Blend about $44.5. This is $0.5 below my round-1 $45: Goldman's cut is no longer fresh and Ma'aden is worth a bit more, but I trim FCF and the multiple from 5.25x to 5.1x. It is $0.4 above the agents' $44.1 mean.
supervisor_summary: After two rounds the five forecasters agree on the pro forma facts (debt $5.42B, cash $0.67B, pension $0.57B, 282.8M shares) and on a fair value of $42-46 (mean $44.1), against a $42 close. My checks found that Goldman's $2,700/t 2027 cut dates from 6 July, not September, and that the Ma'aden stake is worth about $1.43B at market rather than the $1.15-1.25B the agents credit. These lift my reconciled fair value to about $44.5, only about 6% above spot. I leave both ladders at the agents' mean. AA remains a ~50%-vol bet on the aluminium deck at roughly $3.5/share per $100/t, with Q3 results and the South32 vote on 15 Oct and a 34%-priced FOMC hike on 28 Oct inside the month. Round-2 convergence is real on facts but partly anchored on my round-1 template (four agents use the same $1.25B Ma'aden haircut).
key_drivers: Aluminium deck: bank 2027 forecasts of $2,700 (GS, 6 Jul) and ~$2,850 (MS, 8 Jul) were set three months ago, while LME has held about $3,180-3,250. Each $100/t is about $0.2B EBITDA, or about $3.5/share.

Pro forma balance sheet: debt $5.42B, cash $0.67B, pension $0.57B, offset by the Ma'aden stake (86.0M shares, about $1.43B at market, locked until Jul 2028-30 but hedgeable) and about $1.0B FCF to Sep-27.
AliGroup (vote 15 Oct, close H1 2027) adds about $0.72-0.75B through-cycle EBITDA but is alumina-heavy, with alumina at $349-369/t FOB WA near cost.
Midwest premium of $1.09/lb (CFO, 10 Sep) vs the $1.19 record; a Canada tariff deal would cut it but also Alcoa's own tariff cost.
Gulf restart (EGA full by Q1 2027) and Indonesian supply point to a 2027 surplus; China's September ingot draw is seasonal.
